// Run starts dispatching alerts incoming via the updates channel.
func (d *Dispatcher) Run(dispatchStartTime time.Time) {
	d.done = make(chan struct{})

	d.mtx.Lock()
	d.logger.Debug("preparing to start", "startTime", dispatchStartTime)
	d.startTimer = time.NewTimer(time.Until(dispatchStartTime))
	d.state = DispatcherStateWaitingToStart
	d.logger.Debug("setting state", "state", "waiting_to_start")
	d.aggrGroupsPerRoute = map[*Route]map[model.Fingerprint]*aggrGroup{}
	d.aggrGroupsNum = 0
	d.metrics.aggrGroups.Set(0)
	d.ctx, d.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	d.mtx.Unlock()

	d.run(d.alerts.Subscribe("dispatcher"))
	close(d.done)
}

changeset.goal: Restore continuous visibility of active alert groups through the groups API across a valid configuration reload by removing the unserved gap between stopping the old dispatcher and the replacement dispatcher serving aggregation groups.

changes.semantic_action: In the configCoordinator.Subscribe callback in cmd/alertmanager/main.go, reorder the dispatcher lifecycle so the replacement dispatcher is constructed and started before the old dispatcher is stopped: build routes/receivers/pipeline, construct the new dispatcher via dispatch.NewDispatcher, start it with go disp.Run(startTime.Add(*DispatchStartDelay)), and only then call disp.Stop() on the previous dispatcher (guarding for the initial nil dispatcher). The groupFn closure continues to read the current disp pointer, so the groups API must observe a serving dispatcher at every instant. Preserve the existing inhibitor.Stop()/inhibitor.Run() handling and the existing error returns from template/receiver building.
changes.intent: Eliminate the window in which disp is stopped but the replacement dispatcher has not yet populated aggrGroupsPerRoute, so the groups API never observes an empty dispatcher during a valid reload.

postconditions.statement: After a valid Alertmanager configuration reload, active alert groups remain visible through the groups API and do not temporarily disappear from it.
postconditions.planned_check: Run the registered method probe alertmanager-reload-v4 against the local production process and observe the groups API during and immediately after twenty valid reloads.
postconditions.check_scope: Local production process HTTP API groups endpoint; 2ms sampling during twenty valid reloads with 2048 injected groups; no guarantee at unsampled instants or distributed convergence.
postconditions.coverage_rationale: The probe samples the groups API at 2ms intervals during and at return of twenty valid reloads; a failure disproves continuous visibility, but success at sampled instants does not exhaust all unsampled instants or distributed convergence.
semantic_statements: The groups API returns the injected active alert groups at each successful sample during twenty valid reloads.
Immediately after each successful reload response, the groups API contains all injected active alert names.

open_obligations.statement: Continuous visibility of active alert groups at every unsampled instant during a valid reload, and under distributed convergence, remains unverified by the sampled probe.
open_obligations.reason: The registered probe samples at 2ms intervals and does not cover unsampled instants or distributed convergence; the reorder removes the evidenced unserved gap but does not prove absence of any residual gap.
open_obligations.coverage_rationale: The probe's sampled continuity is necessary but not sufficient for the full continuous-visibility statement; unsampled instants and distributed convergence remain open.
semantic_statements: Active alert groups remain visible through the groups API at every instant during a valid reload, including unsampled instants.

precondition_review.condition: Dispatcher.Run initializes aggrGroupsPerRoute to an empty map and only repopulates it asynchronously via alert replay after startTimer fires.
precondition_review.rationale: The reorder relies on the replacement dispatcher being started before the old one is stopped; Run's empty-map initialization is the evidenced reason the old stop must not precede the new start.

precondition_review.condition: Inhibitor.Run establishes its own context and rule caches; the reload callback stops and recreates the inhibitor alongside the dispatcher.
precondition_review.rationale: The reorder must preserve the existing inhibitor.Stop()/inhibitor.Run() lifecycle so inhibition behavior is not regressed while the dispatcher handoff is changed.

precondition_review.condition: Alerts.Subscribe replays the current active alerts into a buffered channel for the new dispatcher's iterator.
precondition_review.rationale: The replacement dispatcher's aggrGroupsPerRoute is repopulated from this replay; the reorder depends on the replay being able to run while the old dispatcher is still serving.

preservation_impact.rationale: CH1 reorders the dispatcher lifecycle in the reload callback, which is the production path that determines whether active alert groups remain visible through the groups API during a valid reload.

// Run starts dispatching alerts incoming via the updates channel.
func (d *Dispatcher) Run(dispatchStartTime time.Time) {
	d.done = make(chan struct{})

	d.mtx.Lock()
	d.logger.Debug("preparing to start", "startTime", dispatchStartTime)
	d.startTimer = time.NewTimer(time.Until(dispatchStartTime))
	d.state = DispatcherStateWaitingToStart
	d.logger.Debug("setting state", "state", "waiting_to_start")
	d.aggrGroupsPerRoute = map[*Route]map[model.Fingerprint]*aggrGroup{}
	d.aggrGroupsNum = 0
	d.metrics.aggrGroups.Set(0)
	d.ctx, d.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	d.mtx.Unlock()

	d.run(d.alerts.Subscribe("dispatcher"))
	close(d.done)
}
